pure-announcement.rationale: It is an analytical essay synthesizing published research into a management framework, not a product or funding announcement.

duplicate.rationale: The supplied nearest concepts are retrieval and MCP notes; none covers comprehension loss from AI-generated code or team mental-model erosion.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The central claims cite specific checkable studies — MIT EEG (arXiv:2506.08872), METR RCT (arXiv:2507.09089), GitClear's longitudinal analysis, Gerlich's survey — plus Naur's theory-building paper.

durability.rationale: The mechanism — teams accumulate code whose theory nobody built, degrading their ability to change systems even when the code is correct — is a Naur-rooted pattern that outlives the individual 2025 studies cited as evidence.

actionability.rationale: It sequences concrete interventions by stakes: budget 20-30% for comprehension, decision logs, three-question theory reviews, design intent before generation, structured comprehension loops, monthly theory rebuilds, and four observable warning signs of existing debt.

atomicity.rationale: Evidence, practices and warning signs all serve the single stateable concept of cognitive debt — the erosion of shared mental models under AI-assisted development.
